# 16岁开音响租赁公司，如今做出年入1500万美元的SaaS：Rentman创始人做对了什么

![封面图](https://images.indiehackers.com/team-images/Roy-van-den-Broek_nl2.jpg)

16岁的你在干什么？

打游戏？

谈恋爱？

备考期末？

Roy 16岁的时候，在当DJ。

还开了一家公司。

不是那种"帮邻居遛狗"的小学生生意。

是真正的音响租赁公司。

音响、灯光、设备。

 weddings，派对，活动。

真刀真枪。

**【问题不是缺想法，是缺好用的工具】**

做生意的时候，问题来了。

市场上的软件，要么是为别的行业做的，硬套过来用。

要么是又贵又难用的"上古软件"。

大家都抱怨，但没人解决。

Roy说：我自己做一个。

他不是想做一家软件公司。

只是想解决自己的问题。

用现在的话说： scratching his own itch（挠自己的痒）。

当时Ruby on Rails刚火。

他现学现卖。

没有宏伟蓝图。

没有商业计划书。

没有团队。

就他一个人，一台电脑，晚上写代码。

**【五个客户，改变了一切】**

软件做好了，自己用着还行。

其他租赁公司听说了，问：能给我们用吗？

五个公司成了早期用户。

Roy没当回事。

心想：做完这个，回去继续租音响呗。

但这五个人不停提需求。

今天这个要改，明天那个要加。

软件越滚越大。

有一天他突然发现——

这事好像比音响租赁更有搞头？

Rentman就这样诞生了。

不是为了改变世界。

就是为了少点麻烦。

**【两个坚持：简单，上云】**

Roy做了两个关键决定。

**第一，简单。**

当时的软件都太复杂了。

界面像飞机仪表盘。

老板们逼员工用，员工恨之入骨。

Roy说：我的软件，不用培训就能用。

**第二，上云。**

那时候2012年左右。

大部分同行的软件都是本地的。

只能在办公室里用。

Roy说：我要让人在任何地方都能工作。

在活动现场。

在家里。

在咖啡厅。

这在当时是革命性的。

**【自举八年，70国用户】**

Rentman做了8年自举（bootstrapping）。

什么意思？

没有拿VC一分钱。

全靠客户付费养活。

用户从几个变成了几万个。

覆盖70多个国家。

Roy从程序员，变成了销售，变成了HR，变成了CEO。

每个阶段都现学。

他说：每次公司到了新阶段，我不适应，就会成为瓶颈。

产品能scale，市场能scale，团队能scale。

但我不一定能scale。

这是他最大的挑战。

也是最大的学费。

**【没有营销预算，怎么增长？】**

你可能以为他们会砸钱做广告。

没有。

他们的增长靠的是三个东西：

**社区。**

活动行业是个小圈子。

大家都在同一个trade show上见面。

互相推荐生意。

Roy花了很多年时间，混这个圈子。

不是作为软件销售，

而是作为行业一份子。

赞助活动。

办webinar。

和用户真聊。

当一个租赁公司向另一个推荐Rentman，

比什么广告都管用。

**自然飞轮。**

自由职业者（freelance crew）给多个租赁公司干活。

这个公司用Rentman，他学会了。

去下一家公司，他说：你们也用Rentman吧，我好上手。

用户自己成了传教士。

**产品驱动增长（PLG）。**

任何人都可以免费试用。

自己注册。

一天内跑通真实项目。

不用销售跟着屁股后面推销。

产品够好，用户自己决定买不买。

**【从100人到管理的艺术】**

团队从几个人变成100多人。

10人的时候，怎么管都成。

50人的时候，不行了。

100人的时候，又不行了。

Roy说：每个阶段都要重新发明管理。

他给了一本书推荐：《Scaling Up》。

说的是公司怎么从中小变大。

但他最重要的领悟是——

不能乱招人。

每次招人都要谨慎。

因为工资是固定成本。

租不起。

**【最后的建议：做你喜欢的事】**

Roy说：如果你做不喜欢的事，撑不下去的。

不是因为难。

是因为难的时间太长了。

Rentman做了十几年。

中间N次想放弃。

但因为喜欢这个行业，

喜欢解决问题，

才熬过来。

他说：就算最后没成功，

至少过程是开心的。

这话听起来像鸡汤。

但当你真的试过——

凌晨三点改bug，

客户打电话骂你，

现金流告急，

你就知道——

没有热爱，

真的扛不住。

**【未来：AI和可能的自我颠覆】**

Rentman现在年收入1500万到2000万美元。

全球市场领导者。

但Roy在想的是AI。

不是用AI做功能。

而是：AI会不会让现在的商业模式过时？

现在的收费是按座位（per-seat）。

如果AI能自动做计划、做报价、做协调，

用户还需要这么多"座位"吗？

Roy说：

"我宁愿自己颠覆自己，

也不想等别人来颠覆我。"

商业模式可能全改。

定价可能全改。

但他准备好了。

**【你有没有这样的觉悟？】**

Roy从16岁的DJ，

到年入千万的SaaS创始人。

没有惊天动地的故事。

就是——

发现问题，

解决问题，

然后一直做下去。

他说：

做你喜欢的事。

不是因为它能赚钱。

而是因为——

你会做很久。

如果不喜欢，

任何一个坎都能拦住你。

如果喜欢的，

十个坎也拦不住。

你呢？

在做喜欢的事吗？

还是只为了钱，

在忍受痛苦？

*P.S. 如果你在活动行业干活，

device租赁、灯光、舞台、视频制作——

去rentman.com看看。

据说能省下你一半的管理时间。*

**

title_en: He started an audio rental company at the age of 16 and now makes US$15 million in annual SaaS: What did the founder of Rentman do right?
title_jp: 16歳でオーディオレンタル会社を始め、現在は年間1500万ドルのSaaSを作る：Rentmanの創設者は正しかったこと
title_ar: افتتحت شركة تأجير الصوت في سن 16 عامًا وتحصل الآن على 15 مليون دولار سنويًا من SaaS: ما الذي فعله مؤسس Rentman بشكل صحيح
content_en:
He started an audio rental company at the age of 16 and now makes US$15 million in annual SaaS: What did the founder of Rentman do right?

What are you doing at 16?

Playing games?

Falling in love?

Final preparation period?

Roy was 16 years old and was working as a DJ.

He also opened a company.

It's not the kind of schoolboy business that "helps neighbors walk their dogs".

It's a real audio rental company.

Sound, lighting, equipment.

 Weddings, parties, events.

Real knives and real guns.

[The problem is not the lack of ideas, but the lack of useful tools]

When doing business, problems arise.

The software on the market is either made for other industries and used hard.

Either it is expensive and difficult to use "ancient software".

Everyone complained, but no one solved it.

Roy said: I made one myself.

He doesn't want to start a software company.

Just trying to solve my own problems.

In today's terms: scratching his own itch.

Ruby on Rails was just popular at the time.

He learns and sells now.

There is no grand blueprint.

There is no business plan.

There is no team.

He was alone, with a computer, writing code at night.

[Five customers changed everything]

The software is ready, but it's okay to use it yourself.

Other leasing companies heard about it and asked: Can we use it?

Five companies became early users.

Roy didn't take it seriously.

I thought to myself: After doing this, I will go back and continue renting stereos.

But these five people kept asking for their needs.

This one will be changed today, and that one will be added tomorrow.

The software is rolling bigger and bigger.

One day he suddenly discovered--

This seems to be more exciting than renting audio?

This is how Rentman was born.

Not to change the world.

Just to avoid trouble.

[Two persistences: Simple, on the cloud]

Roy made two key decisions.

First, simple.

The software at that time was too complex.

The interface is like an airplane dashboard.

Bosses force employees to use it, and employees hate it.

Roy said: My software can be used without training.

Second, go to the clouds.

That was around 2012.

Most of the software from our peers is local.

Can only be used in the office.

Roy said: I want people to work anywhere.

At the event site.

At home.

In the cafe.

This was revolutionary at the time.

[Eight years since self-introduction, users in 70 countries]

Rentman has been bootstrapping for eight years.

What does that mean?

I didn't take a penny from VC.

It is all supported by customers paying for it.

The number of users has changed from a few to tens of thousands.

Covering more than 70 countries.

Roy went from programmer to salesperson, HR, and CEO.

Learn now at every stage.

He said: Every time the company reaches a new stage, I don't adapt and it becomes a bottleneck.

Products can scale, markets can scale, and teams can scale.

But I may not be able to scale.

This is his biggest challenge.

It is also the largest tuition fee.

[How can we grow without a marketing budget?]

You might think they would spend money on advertising.

No.

Their growth depends on three things:

community.

The event industry is a small circle.

Everyone met at the same trade show.

Recommend businesses to each other.

Roy spent many years in this circle.

Not as software sales,

but as part of the industry.

Sponsored activities.

Do webinar.

Really chat with users.

When one rental company recommends Rentman to another,

It works better than any advertising.

Natural flywheel.

Freelance crew works for multiple rental companies.

This company uses Rentman, and he learned it.

Going to the next company, he said: You can also use Rentman, so I can get started.

Users themselves become missionaries.

Product-Driven Growth (PLG).

Anyone can try it for free.

Register yourself.

Run real projects in one day.

Don't have to sell behind you.

If the product is good enough, the user decides whether to buy it or not.

[From 100 people to the art of management]

The team has changed from a few people to more than 100 people.

When there are 10 people, you can manage them any way you want.

When there were 50 people, it couldn't work.

When there were 100 people, it couldn't work again.

Roy said: Management needs to be reinvented at every stage.

He recommended a book: "Scaling Up".

It's about how the company grew from small to medium to large.

But his most important understanding was--

You can't recruit people indiscriminately.

Be careful every time you recruit.

Because wages are fixed costs.

Can't afford it.

[Final advice: Do what you like]

Roy said: If you do something you don't like, you won't be able to survive.

Not because it's difficult.

It's because it's been difficult for too long.

Rentman has been doing it for more than ten years.

I wanted to give up N times in the middle.

But because I like this industry,

Likes to solve problems,

To get through it.

He said: Even if it t succeed in the end,

At least the process was happy.

This sounds like chicken soup.

But when you actually try--

Correcting bugs at 3 a.m.,

Customers call and scold you,

Cash flow is in short supply,

You will know--

Without love,

I really couldn't hold it.

[Future: AI and possible self-disruption]

Rentman now earns $15 million to $20 million a year.

Global market leader.

But Roy was thinking about AI.

It's not using AI for functions.

But: Will AI make current business models obsolete?

The current charge is per-seat.

If AI can automatically make plans, quotations, and coordination,

Do users still need so many "seats"?

Roy said:

"I would rather subvert myself,

I don't want to wait for others to subvert me. "

The business model may be completely changed.

Pricing may change completely.

But he was ready.

[Do you have such awareness?]

Roy went from 16-old DJ,

SaaS founder who earns tens of millions of dollars by the year.

There are no earth-shattering stories.

That is--

Find problems and

Solve problems,

and keep doing it.

He said:

Do what you love.

Not because it makes money.

but because--

You will do it for a long time.

If you t like it,

Any obstacle can stop you.

If you like it,

Ten obstacles cannot stop it.

What about you?

Doing something you like?

Or just for money,

Suffering?

*P.S. If you work in the event industry,

device rental, lighting, stage, video production--

Check out rentman.com.

It is said to save you half of your management time. *

**
